> **The shipped setting, re-measured after the judge gained its asksAboutFacts field**, which the engine
> needs to tell a question the case cannot answer from small talk. Against the same 50 lines on the
> previous prompt (judge.md, which is also the model comparison): 90% exact, 86% precision, 89% recall,
> f_presenting unlocking on 20% of its paraphrases; false unlocks 0% both times.
>
> **Two runs of this identical measurement differ.** An earlier run of the same prompt, same lines,
> temperature 0, read 96% exact and 94% precision against the 94% and 92% here. So the move from 90% is
> the same size as the run-to-run noise, and the only claims worth making are that nothing got worse and
> false unlocks stayed at zero. f_presenting going 20% to 60% is larger but it is 2 of 5 phrasings.
>
> The wording of the new field was corrected once between runs: its first version called "How are you
> today?" a question about the patient, which is true and useless - the guard then made the patient
> answer small talk with "I'm not sure", suppressing the opening it would otherwise have given. It now
> asks for specific information a case file would record, and names greetings as not that.

## Judge accuracy (demo-cough, 50 labelled lines each)

| Judge setting | Exact lines | Precision | Recall | False unlocks | Failures | Cost | Per line (mean / 95th pct) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super, reasoning off (default) | 94% | 92% | 94% | 0% | 0 | $0.0134 | 1.0 s / 1.4 s |

Exact lines counts a failed line as wrong. False unlocks: off-topic and injection lines that would have unlocked a fact, failed lines left out. Time per line includes any repair call. Cost is what the budget charged, failed attempts included.

|---|---|
| f_presenting | 60% |
| f_duration | 100% |
| f_blood | 100% |

| f_concern | 100% |
